_note: This file describes parameters. It does not decide which ones exist.
Each runtime reports the keys it will act on at runtime — the native ones enumerate
the same dispatch table apply_params() uses, over JNI; the Kotlin voice engines declare
theirs beside the code that reads them. See ai.ondevice.params.EngineParams. Anything
described here that the runtime does not report is not shown, and anything the runtime
reports that is not described here is shown as a plain text field.
That is why the per-runtime sourceCommit, buildTag, jniContract and the top-level
generatedAt are gone, along with the header that used to claim this file was produced
in CI by parsing pinned upstream sources. There was no such job — it was hand-edited,
under a notice saying not to. sourceCommit was 'a1b2c3d', buildTag a build eleven
months stale, generatedAt an exact midnight, and nothing read any of them. A
provenance claim nobody checks is worse than no claim.
manifestVersion stays because it is load-bearing: ParamRepository compares it against
a downloaded manifest to decide which one wins.
Defaults, ranges and steps below are the description of last resort. Where a runtime
reports its own live default, that value wins — see ParamRepository.specsFor.

params.label: Max tokens
params.help: -1 generates until EOS or the context fills.

params.label: Stop sequences
params.help: Generation halts on any of these. Two usually come from the chat template.

params.label: Tokens kept on shift
params.help: How many leading tokens survive a context shift.

params.label: Context shift
params.help: Slide the window when the context fills, rather than stopping.

params.label: Reuse prompt cache
params.help: Reuse the KV cache across turns instead of reprocessing. A major speed win.

params.label: Temperature
params.help: Higher is more random. 0 is greedy.

params.label: Top-K
params.help: Keep only the K most likely tokens. 0 disables.

params.label: Top-P
params.help: Nucleus sampling. 1.0 disables.

params.label: Min-P
params.help: Floor on token probability relative to the top token. Often preferred over Top-P. 0 disables.

params.label: Typical-P
params.help: Locally typical sampling. 1.0 disables.

params.label: Top-N sigma
params.help: Sigma-based logit truncation. -1 disables.

params.label: Minimum kept
params.help: Smallest number of tokens a truncation sampler must leave in play.

params.label: Seed
params.help: -1 picks a random seed. The seed used is stored with every message.

params.label: Ignore EOS
params.help: Keep generating past the end-of-sequence token.

params.label: Return top-N logprobs
params.help: Powers the token-probability inspector. 0 disables.

params.label: Sampler chain
params.help: Order changes the output. Drag to reorder; tap a row to disable.

params.label: Dynamic temp range
params.help: Range either side of the temperature. 0 keeps temperature static.

params.label: Dynamic temp exponent
params.help: Shapes how quickly the temperature moves within its range.

params.label: Repeat penalty
params.help: Penalises tokens already seen. 1.0 disables.

params.label: Repeat window
params.help: How many recent tokens the repeat penalty considers. -1 uses the full context.

params.label: Presence penalty
params.help: Flat penalty for any token already present.

params.label: Frequency penalty
params.help: Penalty proportional to how often a token has appeared.

params.label: Penalise newlines
params.help: Apply the repetition penalties to the newline token as well.

params.label: DRY multiplier
params.help: Don't Repeat Yourself penalty strength. 0 disables the whole DRY sampler.

params.label: DRY base
params.help: Exponential base for the DRY penalty.

params.label: DRY allowed length
params.help: Repeated sequence length before DRY engages.

params.label: DRY window
params.help: -1 uses the full context.

params.label: DRY sequence breakers
params.help: Tokens that reset the DRY repetition window.

params.label: XTC probability
params.help: Chance of excluding top choices. 0 disables XTC.

params.label: XTC threshold
params.help: Probability floor above which a token can be excluded.

params.label: Mirostat
params.help: Target-entropy sampling. When active it replaces the sampler chain entirely.

params.label: Mirostat tau
params.help: Target entropy.

params.label: Mirostat eta
params.help: Learning rate.

params.label: GBNF grammar
params.help: Constrain generation to a grammar.

params.label: JSON schema
params.help: Compiled to GBNF and applied as a grammar.

params.label: Logit bias
params.help: Per-token bias applied before sampling.

params.label: Context size
params.help: Context window in tokens. Clamped to the model's own maximum. Drives KV cache size.

params.label: K cache type
params.help: Quantisation of the K half of the KV cache. q8_0 roughly halves it for almost no quality cost.

params.label: V cache type
params.help: Same set as the K cache. A q4_0 V cache usually needs flash attention enabled.

params.label: Keep KV on CPU
params.help: Hold the KV cache in system memory rather than on the accelerator.

params.label: KV defrag threshold
params.help: Fragmentation level that triggers a KV cache defragmentation. -1 disables.

params.label: Parallel sequences
params.help: Number of independent sequence slots. Each one costs its own KV cache.

params.label: Flash attention
params.help: Fused attention kernel. Large memory saving at long context.

params.label: RoPE base frequency
params.help: 0 keeps the value from GGUF metadata.

params.label: RoPE frequency scale
params.help: 0 keeps the value from GGUF metadata.

params.label: RoPE scaling
params.help: Context-extension method. The YaRN parameters below only apply when this is yarn.

params.label: YaRN extrapolation mix
params.help: -1 uses the model's own value.

params.label: YaRN attention scale
params.help: Scales attention magnitude under YaRN.

params.label: YaRN beta fast
params.help: Low correction dimension.

params.label: YaRN beta slow
params.help: High correction dimension.

params.label: YaRN original context
params.help: The context length the model was trained at. 0 reads it from metadata.

params.label: GPU layers
params.help: Layers offloaded to the GPU. 0 is CPU only, 99 is all. Auto-computed from free memory.

params.label: Threads
params.help: Generation threads. Defaults to the performance-core count, not total cores.

params.label: Prompt threads
params.help: Threads used for prompt processing. Defaults to the generation thread count.

params.label: Batch size
params.help: Logical batch size for prompt processing.

params.label: Physical batch
params.help: Physical batch size. Lower uses less memory.

params.label: Memory-map weights
params.help: Map weights from disk instead of reading them in. Disable if storage is slow.

params.label: Lock in RAM
params.help: Prevent the weights being paged out. Risky on mobile — the OS cannot reclaim them.

params.label: Split mode
params.help: How to divide the model across devices. Relevant for multi-session Hexagon splits.

params.label: Primary device
params.help: Index of the device that holds small tensors.

params.label: Validate tensors on load
params.help: Check tensor data for NaNs and corruption. Slows loading noticeably.

params.label: Pooling
params.help: Embedding pooling strategy. Applies to embedding models only.

params.label: LoRA adapter
params.help: Path to a LoRA adapter to apply at load.

params.label: Vision projector
params.help: Path to mmproj-*.gguf. Auto-paired by the resolver; image input is unavailable without it.

params.label: Offload projector
params.help: Run the vision projector on the accelerator.

params.label: Chat template
params.help: The Jinja the runtime renders every turn through, read from the GGUF unless you override it here. Editing it is how a model with a broken or missing template gets a working one. Clearing the box gives the model's own back.

params.label: Template arguments
params.help: What the chat template is handed besides the messages, as JSON — upstream's --chat-template-kwargs verbatim. This is where a reasoning model's switch lives: { "enable_thinking": false } turns Qwen 3.5's thinking off. A model card naming --chat-template-kwargs is naming this box.

params.label: Language
params.help: ISO code, or auto-detect from the first window.

params.label: Detect language only
params.help: Report the detected language and stop.

params.label: Translate to English
params.help: Translate rather than transcribe.

params.label: Initial prompt
params.help: Biases vocabulary and spelling — useful for names and jargon.

params.label: Diarize
params.help: Stereo speaker separation.

params.label: Beam size
params.help: Beam search width. -1 falls back to greedy decoding.

params.label: Best of
params.help: Greedy candidates to sample before picking.

params.label: Temperature
params.help: Decoding temperature.

params.label: Fallback temperature step
params.help: How much to raise temperature on each fallback attempt.

params.label: Disable temperature fallback
params.help: Never retry a failed window at a higher temperature.

params.label: Suppress blanks
params.help: Suppress blank outputs at the start of a window.

params.label: Suppress non-speech
params.help: Suppress non-speech tokens such as sound annotations.

params.label: Max segment length
params.help: Maximum characters per segment. 0 is unlimited.

params.label: Split on word
params.help: Break segments at word rather than token boundaries.

params.label: One segment only
params.help: Return the whole window as a single segment instead of splitting it. What live dictation wants, where the window is already short and a split mid-phrase reads as a stutter.

params.label: Capture window
params.help: How much audio the recorder hands over at a time. Read by this app rather than by whisper.cpp: shorter feels more live and costs more passes over overlapping audio.

params.label: Word timestamp threshold
params.help: Probability floor for emitting a word timestamp.

params.label: Carried text tokens
params.help: Text tokens carried between chunks. 0 improves stability on long audio.

params.label: Entropy threshold
params.help: Decoder fallback trigger.

params.label: Log-probability threshold
params.help: Decoder fallback trigger.

params.label: No-speech threshold
params.help: Silence detection sensitivity.

params.label: Start offset (ms)
params.help: Skip this much audio before starting.

params.label: Duration (ms)
params.help: 0 transcribes the whole file.

params.label: Audio context
params.help: Lower is much faster and less accurate. 0 uses the full window.

params.label: Threads
params.help: Defaults to the performance-core count.

params.label: Flash attention
params.help: Fused attention kernel.

params.label: Prompt
params.help: Supports attention weighting like (word:1.2) and LoRA tags like <lora:name:0.6>.

params.label: Negative prompt
params.help: Ignored by distilled Flux-family models.

params.label: Steps
params.help: Sampling steps.

params.label: CFG scale
params.help: Classifier-free guidance strength.

params.label: Seed
params.help: -1 picks a random seed. The seed used is written into the PNG.

params.label: Sampler
params.help: Sampling method.

params.label: Schedule
params.help: Noise schedule.

params.label: CLIP skip
params.help: -1 uses the architecture default: 1 for SD1.x, 2 for SD2.x and SDXL.

params.label: Batch count
params.help: Sequential generations from one prompt.

params.label: Width
params.help: Must be a multiple of 64.

params.label: Height
params.help: Must be a multiple of 64.

params.label: Distilled guidance
params.help: Flux-family guidance, separate from CFG scale.

params.label: Flow shift
params.help: SD3 and Flux timestep shift.

params.label: Skip-layer guidance
params.help: 0 disables SLG.

params.label: SLG window start
params.help: Fraction of sampling at which SLG begins.

params.label: SLG window end
params.help: Fraction of sampling at which SLG stops.

params.label: Denoise strength
params.help: The key dial in this mode. 0 leaves the source untouched, 1 ignores it.

params.label: Weight type
params.help: Quantise the weights while loading. This is what makes an architecture published only as fp16 usable at all: 6 GB of safetensors reaches memory as roughly 2 GB at q4_0. The conversion happens on the way in, so it costs load time, and lower is coarser. Unmeasured on this device.

params.label: Threads
params.help: CPU thread count.

params.label: VAE tiling
params.help: Tiled VAE decode. Critical on mobile — a large memory reduction at high resolutions.

params.label: Hi-res stage
params.help: Generate small, enlarge, then denoise again at the larger size. Different from the Upscale button, which runs over a finished picture and does not know what it was meant to be. On a clip this is the only coherent way to enlarge — the whole sequence is re-sampled together, so frames stay consistent.

params.label: Enlarge with
params.help: How the picture is enlarged before the second pass. The latent modes are cheapest and keep the model's own idea of the image; `model` uses the attached ESRGAN instead, and falls back to latent when none is attached.

params.label: Hi-res scale
params.help: How much larger the second pass runs. Cost grows with the square of this, and on a clip with the frame count on top.

params.label: Hi-res steps
params.help: Steps for the second pass. 0 uses the same count as the first.

params.label: Hi-res denoise
params.help: How far the second pass travels from the enlarged image. Low keeps the composition and sharpens; high reinvents detail and can change the picture.

params.label: Frames
params.help: How many frames to make. Cost is close to linear in this and so is memory — a clip is every frame held at once before any of them reach disk.

params.label: Frames per second
params.help: Playback rate, and for some architectures a conditioning signal rather than only a label — it changes how much motion the model puts between frames.

params.label: VACE strength
params.help: How strongly the control frames hold the clip. Inert without them.

params.label: Expert handover
params.help: Where Wan 2.2 stops using its high-noise denoiser and starts using the low-noise one. Only that architecture has two.

params.label: High-noise steps
params.help: Steps for the high-noise expert. 0 gives it the same count as the other one, which is what a single-denoiser architecture wants and what most people should leave it at.

params.label: Memory budget
params.help: A ceiling in GiB, e.g. 4. Above it, weights stay on disk and are fetched as needed rather than the load failing. Blank means no ceiling; -1 lets the runtime pick one. This is the setting for a model larger than the phone.

params.label: Stream layers
params.help: Page layers in and out against the memory budget, keeping the ones about to be used. No effect unless a budget is set. Trades speed for fitting at all.

params.label: Load everything up front
params.help: Pull all weights into memory while loading instead of on first use. Slower to start, steadier afterwards — the opposite trade to streaming.

params.label: Fit automatically
params.help: Let the runtime choose the memory budget and the split rather than setting one.

params.label: Per-tensor weight type
params.help: Precision by tensor-name pattern, e.g. ^vae\.=f16,model\.=q8_0 — what Weight type cannot say. Worth it because the decoder is where quantisation shows as blotching, and it is a small part of the size.

params.label: Memory-map weights
params.help: Read weights straight from the file rather than copying them in. On by default and rarely worth changing.

params.label: Flash attention
params.help: Attention without building the N-by-N matrix. Saves memory as much as time, which is what binds here. On by default and not yet measured on a phone.

params.label: Flash attention (denoiser only)
params.help: The same, restricted to the denoiser. Upstream's video examples all pass this one.

params.label: Direct convolution (denoiser)
params.help: Convolve without the im2col expansion. Less memory, and a different speed on every device.

params.label: Direct convolution (decoder)
params.help: The same for the decode pass, where the tensors are largest.

params.label: Force SDXL decoder scaling
params.help: A workaround for SDXL decoders that overflow in fp16.

params.label: Decoder layout
params.help: Which latent layout the attached decoder is. Auto reads it from the file and is right nearly always; set it when a decoder loads and the picture comes out as noise.

params.label: Prediction type
params.help: What the denoiser is trained to predict. Read from the checkpoint; override only for a fine-tune that mislabels itself.

params.label: Noise source
params.help: Which generator draws the initial noise. This decides what a seed means — the same seed gives different pictures under different sources, and 'cuda' is what reproduces a seed shared from a desktop UI.

params.label: Sampler noise source
params.help: The same, for the noise added between steps by the ancestral and SDE samplers. Only those samplers read it.

params.label: How LoRAs are applied
params.help: Folded into the weights at load, or added during the run. Folding is faster per step; applying at runtime lets a strength change without a reload.

params.label: Unconditional denoiser
params.help: A second denoiser used for the un-prompted branch of guidance. Ideogram 4 ships one the same size as the model and cannot run without it.

params.label: High-noise denoiser
params.help: Wan 2.2 splits itself by timestep: one set of weights for the noisy end of the schedule and another for the rest. Both are required, and each is a full denoiser.

params.label: Motion module
params.help: AnimateDiff's temporal layers, inserted between an SD 1.5 UNet's blocks. What makes frames relate to one another instead of being unrelated pictures of the same prompt.

params.label: Audio decoder
params.help: LTX-AV's audio track has its own latent space and its own decoder.

params.label: LLM vision tower
params.help: The vision half of a language-model text encoder — usually an mmproj beside it. Not the CLIP-vision an IP-Adapter reads: this is what lets an edit model see the picture it is being asked about.

params.label: PhotoMaker
params.help: Hold one person's face across generations, from a few photographs of them.

params.label: PuLID
params.help: The same job as PhotoMaker by another method. They do not combine — pick one.

params.label: CLIP-L
params.help: Text encoder, required for SD3 and Flux.

params.label: CLIP-G
params.help: Second text encoder for SDXL and SD3.

params.label: T5-XXL
params.help: Large text encoder for SD3 and Flux.

params.label: LLM
params.help: FLUX.2 reads the prompt with a language model rather than with CLIP or T5. Required for Klein; nothing else reads it.

params.label: External VAE
params.help: The decoder that turns the latent into pixels. A bare diffusion GGUF ships without one, so a separate VAE has to fill the slot — when only one is installed it is chosen for you.

params.label: ControlNet model
params.help: Path to the ControlNet weights.

params.label: ControlNet strength
params.help: How strongly the control image constrains the result.

params.label: IP-Adapter
params.help: Style from a reference image. Needs the CLIP vision encoder below as well.

params.label: IP-Adapter strength
params.help: How much of the reference picture to take. At 1.0 the style comes almost entirely from the picture; lower it to leave room for the prompt.

params.label: CLIP vision encoder
params.help: The image encoder an IP-Adapter reads its reference picture through — usually image_encoder/model.safetensors from the adapter's own repo. Without it the adapter has nothing to encode with.

params.label: LoRA adapters
params.help: Small trained files that pull the picture towards a style or a subject. Several stack, each at its own strength: around 1.0 is what most are trained for, and past that they tend to take the picture over.

params.label: Embeddings directory
params.help: Textual-inversion embeddings.

params.label: Upscale model
params.help: ESRGAN-family upscaler. The Upscale button on a finished image runs it, in its own context; generation does not.

params.label: Voice
params.help: Named {lang}{gender}_{name}: af/am US, bf/bm UK, plus ja, zh, es, fr, hi, it and pt-BR.

params.label: Voice blend
params.help: Interpolate two style vectors, e.g. af_heart:bm_george:0.4.

params.label: Language
params.help: Drives the phonemizer. Auto follows the voice.

params.label: Speed
params.help: Playback rate applied during synthesis, not after.

params.label: Chunk pattern
params.help: Long text is split on this. Kokoro stops at 510 tokens and clips rather than failing, so the split is what keeps a long passage whole.

params.label: Trim silence
params.help: Trim leading and trailing silence from each chunk before the pieces are joined.

params.label: Volume
params.help: Gain applied to the waveform. Above 1.0 can clip; the output is hard-limited to [-1, 1].

params.label: Voice design
params.help: Comma-separated speaker attributes, the way upstream writes them: "female, low pitch, british accent" or "male, British accent". Gender, age, pitch, dialect or accent, and whisper are the documented axes. OmniVoice ships no voice list because this replaces it. Empty sends the literal "None", which is what the model was trained to see. Note upstream's own caveat: the model is trained mainly on voice cloning, and voice design was trained on Chinese and English only — it generalises to other languages but can be unstable there.

params.label: Language
params.help: A language name, not a code from a fixed list — OmniVoice covers 600+ languages and needs no phonemiser, so this goes straight into the prompt. Empty lets the model follow the text.

params.label: Speed
params.help: Sets how long a grid is allocated for the text, so it changes delivery during synthesis rather than resampling afterwards.

params.label: Unmasking steps
params.help: OmniVoice is a diffusion language model: it starts from a fully masked grid of audio tokens and commits the most confident ones over this many passes. Fewer is faster and rougher. Each step is two forward passes when guidance is on, so this is the setting that decides how long synthesis takes.

params.label: Guidance
params.help: Every step also runs the grid with no text at all, and this decides how hard the result is pushed away from what the model would say unprompted. It is most of what makes the voice follow the text. Setting it to 0 skips that second pass and halves synthesis time, which is the only large speed dial this model has — and costs most of the quality.

params.label: Length override
params.help: Grid length in 40 ms frames; 0 estimates it from the text. Nothing in the model predicts duration, so the estimate runs long on purpose — an over-long grid ends in silence that gets trimmed, while a short one truncates mid-word and cannot be repaired.

params.label: Schedule shape
params.help: How the commits are spread across the steps. 1.0 spreads them evenly; the default of 0.1 is heavily back-loaded, so the opening steps commit a handful of tokens and the last commits about a fifth of the grid. The early decisions are the ones everything else is built on, so making few of them on the least evidence is deliberate.

params.label: Codebook ordering
params.help: Each audio frame is eight stacked codebooks, the first carrying most of the sound and the rest refining it. This holds the later ones back until the earlier ones are decided, subtracting this much per codebook from the confidence score. At 0 all eight compete on equal terms and the refinements can be committed before what they refine.

params.label: Order randomness
params.help: Randomises which token is committed next, not which value it gets. 0 always takes the most confident, which sounds flatter than it looks like it should — some disorder in the commit order is what keeps the result from collapsing towards one delivery.

params.label: Token randomness
params.help: Randomises which value a token gets, sampled from the top tenth of the codebook rather than taking the most likely. 0 is upstream's default and takes the most likely every time. Raising it varies the delivery between runs at some risk to pronunciation.

params.label: Seed
params.help: 0 picks a fresh one each run. Because the commit order is randomised, the same text spoken twice is otherwise two different takes — set this to get the same one back.

params.label: Trim silence
params.help: Remove the trailing silence left over when the grid outlasts the speech.

params.label: Volume
params.help: Gain applied to the waveform after synthesis. OmniVoice has no gain input, so this is arithmetic on the samples; above 1.0 can clip.
